transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Tran (AE, Redwood), Marcus Bell (SE, Redwood), James Patel (Head of ML, Clara Health), Rebecca Li (SRE Lead), Tom Andrews (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick scoping to lock the go/no-go thresholds for the POC, validate workload sizing (QPS/concurrency), and agree on reporting format for acceptance. Plan is to run a 2-week benchmark sprint with defined pass/fail gates (latency, accuracy, error rate, cost).

Topics covered:
- Success criteria (latency p95, accuracy/F1, error budget)
- Load profile and dataset size for bench runs
- Reporting template and ownership
- Security/placement constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2 artifacts)
- Timeline and next steps for pilot gating

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia Tran: Hey every, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda -- we wanna lock the go no go rubrick and the load plan so engineering can, um, run the sprint next week.
[00:18] James Patel: Yep, thanks Alicia. we have three main success signals: latency under our p95 target, labeling accuracy for NERF — sorry named entity extraction — F1 above threshold, and cost per thousand tokens under a cap.
[00:35] Marcus Bell: cool, can I clarify the target numbers? you mentioned p95 150ms in email but is that end-to-end or just inference?
[00:47] James Patel: that's end-to-end for our API, so includes network hop. if that's too tight we can scope to inference-p95 then add a headroom multiplier.
[01:05] Rebecca Li: network wise we need VPC peering for the private runs and KMS for key management; SOC2 compliance is a must — we'll need audit logs.
[01:20] Alicia Tran: totally. for the POC we typically run both hosted baseline and dedicated/private testing. baseline will be on Redwood hosted so we can compare. for private we'll need the peering info.
[01:36] Tom Andrews: procurement question — is there a short term trial or do we need a purchase order before dedicated capacity?
[01:45] Marcus Bell: for dedicated we usually do a trial reservation; contract team handles PO but we can start tests on hosted while procurement completes paperwork.
[02:02] James Patel: okay good. about the accuracy metric — our internal eval uses macro-F1 and a human pass rate. we'd like F1 >= 0.88 and human pass >= 92% to consider it acceptable.
[02:18] Marcus Bell: noted. in our experience with similar workloads that F1 is doable with right prompt engineering and quantization profile, but the latency tradeoff depends on model size and batching.
[02:34] Alicia Tran: which leads to load sizing — can you confirm expected QPS and concurrency for the production sim?
[02:43] James Patel: production is roughly 120 reqs/s peak, sustained 60 reqs/s, with median payloads around 450 tokens; concurrency expected ~20ish. for the POC we want two phases: functional (small batch 2k requests) and load (3-hour window ramp to 120 qps).
[03:05] Rebecca Li: also thread about KV cache behavior — our flows are chatty and cache hit rate will matter. we want to measure effective token reduction from prefix caching.
[03:19] Marcus Bell: yep we will instrument KV cache metrics; sometimes the transcription calls it kayvy cache in logs, so heads up.
[03:28] James Patel: ha, kayvy. fine.
[03:32] Alicia Tran: ok for the benchmark runbook our suggested pass/fail rubric:
[03:39] - Latency: inference-p95 < 120ms OR end-to-end p95 < 200ms depending on host vs private
[03:48] - Accuracy: NER F1 >= 0.88 and human pass >= 92%
[03:56] - Error rate: < 0.5% 5xxs or model failures
[04:02] - Cost: incremental per-1k token cost below $X (we'll put exact number in spreadsheet)
[04:10] James Patel: that looks reasonable. can we also include a regression tolerance — like if accuracy drops more than 1.5% vs baseline we consider a fail?
[04:21] Marcus Bell: yes we can capture delta vs baseline. we'll run a baseline on the hosted model family and then validate on the dedicated quantized variant.
[04:31] Rebecca Li: for private we need to confirm HSM/KMS access times won't add latency. if KMS adds a round trip per request that's a non-starter.
[04:44] Alicia Tran: agreed. we'll instrument KMS latency separately and annotate in report. for the POC we'll run both with KMS enabled and disabled to quantify the delta.
[04:56] James Patel: timeline question — you said two-week sprint; do we get full benchmarks and reporting by the end of week two?
[05:04] Marcus Bell: target is: week 0 (this week) get samples & env access; week 1 run baseline functional + fix issues; week 2 run load and produce final report. final report by EOD week 2.
[05:18] Tom Andrews: procurement still wants a formal signoff doc with acceptance criteria for finance to greenlight. can you produce that?
[05:26] Alicia Tran: yes we will produce an acceptance packet: rubric, runbook, artifact list, and a summary deck. we'll share as a single PDF and Google sheet for metrics.
[05:37] James Patel: regarding reporting format — we want CSV of raw traces, a summarized dashboard, and pass/fail table. human annotation samples attached.
[05:47] Marcus Bell: ok we'll include raw traces, p95/p50/p99 histograms, error logs, and sample responses with scoring.
[05:56] Rebecca Li: slight concern: what about cold-starts and model swap behavior? we need to see warm vs cold latency breakdown.
[06:05] Marcus Bell: good call, we'll annotate cold-starts, and include KV cache warmup curve.
[06:12] James Patel: on the dataset, we'll provide 2,000 anonymized requests with golden labels. is that enough?
[06:18] Alicia Tran: for functional checks yeah. for load we want a synthetic generator to reach 120 qps for the 3-hour window; Marcus will share config.
[06:28] Marcus Bell: i'll put together a replay script that replays requests with timestamp jitter to emulate production. also include token length distribution.
[06:38] Tom Andrews: and SLAs — after POC what typical SLA targets do you see customers get?
[06:44] Alicia Tran: enterprise SLA typically 99.9% uptime and 95th or 99th tail latency commitments depending on plan; we'll include example SLA language but procurement will want legal review.
[06:56] James Patel: any competitors we should be aware of? we asked Anthropic and also ran internal eval on Bedrock prototypes.
[07:05] Marcus Bell: noted — we'll include comparative notes but not a formal benchmark vs competitors for this POC.
[07:12] Rebecca Li: security checklist — please send SOC2 report and our security team will run a short questionnaire.
[07:19] Alicia Tran: will do, Alicia to share SOC2, privacy whitepaper, and a checklist.
[07:24] James Patel: ok about go/no-go decision — who signs off on the acceptance? engineering or business?
[07:31] Tom Andrews: procurement needs business sign off plus legal; final acceptance will be a joint signoff: Head of ML and VP Product or procurement depending on dollar value.
[07:41] Alicia Tran: great. we'll draft an acceptance signature block in the packet.
[07:45] Marcus Bell: a couple of technical caveats: quantized models may have slight accuracy delta; we'll include a conversion table for model size vs latency vs cost. sometimes quantization yields 1% accuracy drop.
[07:58] James Patel: that's fine as long as we see the deltas.
[08:03] Rebecca Li: one more infra ask — are logs retained and accessible for 30 days? we need retention policy in writing.
[08:10] Alicia Tran: default retention is 90 days for the POC logs; we'll include retention config and export steps.
[08:18] Marcus Bell: action items recap: i'll share load generator, Alicia will share runbook and security artifacts, James to upload samples.
[08:26] James Patel: timeline recap from our side — upload samples by Mon 5/24, Rebecca will follow up on peering details, Tom will push procurement timeline to Alicia.
[08:36] Tom Andrews: yep, I'll try to get PO template by end of next week.
[08:41] Alicia Tran: perfect. we'll aim to start functional runs 5/25 and full load 6/1 pending access.
[08:49] Marcus Bell: any other blockers?
[08:52] Rebecca Li: none on my side once I get the peering checklist.
[08:56] James Patel: none.
[08:59] Alicia Tran: awesome, thanks all. we'll send the packet today and follow up in thread.
[09:05] (call ends)

Appendix - agreed POC acceptance table (in words):
- Functional pass: run 2k labeled tests, F1 >= 0.88 and human pass >= 92%
- Load pass: ramp to 120 qps for 3 hours, inference-p95 < 120ms (or end-to-end p95 < 200ms) and error rate < 0.5%
- Cost gate: incremental cost under target (exact number in spreadsheet)
- Security gate: VPC peering confirmed, KMS access validated, SOC2 docs provided

References / shared artifacts mentioned:
- Benchmark runbook (Redwood link)
- Metrics spreadsheet (to be shared)
- Security questionnaire (Redwood security pack)
